A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iLRM research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Content can be matched despite substantial reformatting and section renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction, efficiency, generalization, and ablation results on RE10K, ACID, and DL3DV, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds depth, geometry, camera-pose robustness, attention visualization, and scalability evaluations.

M1.justification: The viewpoint tokenization, per-view cross-attention, global self-attention, token uplifting, mini-batch attention, Gaussian decoder, and training loss remain unchanged. The added optimization interpretation and implementation disclosures do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds Tanks&Temples and Mip-NeRF360 evaluations for novel-view synthesis and depth, plus NRGBD and ETH3D pointmap evaluations. It also introduces corrupted-camera-input scenarios. This substantially extends the original RE10K, ACID, and DL3DV coverage beyond image synthesis into geometric accuracy and imperfect inputs.

E2.justification: Mip-Splatting is removed from the 16-view and 32-view wide-coverage comparisons in Table 5. The other principal reconstruction comparators remain. MoGe-2 supplies pseudo-depth reference targets rather than serving as a newly evaluated reconstruction baseline.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a 51-scene DL3DV evaluation split, tests 32-view-trained models with unseen view counts, and adds depth, pointmap, and translation-noise protocols. Geometry evaluation specifies an F1 threshold of 0.1 and downsampling ground-truth pointmaps for iLRM. Long-LRM is explicitly re-evaluated using released checkpoints except for 16-view metrics. Reported AdamW beta2 changes from 0.095 to 0.95, without establishing that training was rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds layerwise attention-correspondence analysis, camera-translation perturbation tests, generalization beyond the training view count, and latency scaling through 256 views. It extends post-prediction optimization analysis to additional datasets. These investigate mechanisms and robustness beyond the retained architectural, overlap, and representation-density ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new Gaussian-noise standard deviations specify input perturbations, not uncertainty in estimated results.

E6.justification: Numerous new results accompany the added evaluations. Retained eight-view MC results also change: Table 1 RE10K PSNR increases numerically from 30.96 to 31.24, and Table 2 ACID/DL3DV PSNR changes from 30.47/29.03 to 30.72/29.33. Table 5 revises baseline results: 32-view 3D-GS PSNR changes from 23.60 to 24.43, while iLRM remains 24.30. Its timings and Long-LRM results are revised, and the 50-epoch iLRM row is removed; these should not be interpreted as demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The model equations, training objective, and FLOPs calculation are retained. v3's added approximate-gradient expressions illustrate the existing optimization analogy; they introduce no defined energy function, formal guarantee, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The three central architectural contributions remain unchanged. The introduction narrows the wide-coverage claim from outperforming optimization-based 3D-GS in reconstruction quality to achieving comparable performance in approximately 0.5 seconds versus approximately eight minutes.

C2.justification: v3 clarifies refinement under fixed image evidence and interprets attention visualizations as progressive correspondence formation. It adds static-scene and geometry-supervision limitations, explicitly qualifies pseudo-depth agreement as indirect evidence, and attributes faster post-prediction optimization partly to geometric quality. The original scalability and camera-pose limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies 50,000 high-resolution fine-tuning iterations, post-prediction optimization learning rates, and Long-LRM checkpoint provenance, while correcting the reported AdamW beta2. It removes v2's explicit training disclosure of FlashAttention-2, BFloat16, and gradient-checkpointing use. The project-page destination is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Perceiver, sparse transformers, state-space alternatives, MoGe-2, DUSt3R, Rayzer, FLARE, and newly evaluated benchmarks. Mip-Splatting and several implementation references disappear. The principal related-work discussion is substantially retained from v2 Appendix A, now in main Section 2.

P1.justification: Related work moves into the main text, experimental-setup subsections become condensed run-in paragraphs, and several method explanations are shortened. Affiliation and acknowledgement text also changes. The existing introduction, method narrative, ablation explanations, and conclusion largely retain their structure and wording.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the single-column presentation with a two-column layout and substantially reorganizes tables and illustrations. It adds attention, depth, geometry, and optimization visualizations plus new evaluation tables. Existing displays are also resized, reordered, or relocated; for example, v2 Figure 7's high-resolution comparison becomes v3 Figure 15.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for reconstruction quality and scalability by testing previously unmeasured geometry, pose-error sensitivity, and behavior beyond the training view count. The revised 3D-GS comparison and narrower introduction claim improve calibration. Proxy-depth dependence, method-specific pointmap downsampling, and removal of Mip-Splatting limit some comparisons, but the broader validation and clearer applicability boundaries provide a substantial net improvement over v2.
